content: Swiss-Prot is a meticulously curated biological database that contains protein sequences. It was established in 1986 by Amos Bairoch during his PhD studies and has been further developed by the Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics and the European Bioinformatics Institute. The primary goal of Swiss-Prot is to provide accurate and reliable protein sequences that are accompanied by extensive annotations. These annotations include detailed descriptions of protein functions, domain structures, post-translational modifications, and sequence variants, among other features. The database also aims to minimize redundancy and ensure a high degree of integration with other biological databases. In 2002, the UniProt consortium was formed as a collaborative effort between the Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics, the European Bioinformatics Institute, and the Protein Information Resource (PIR). This initiative is funded by the National Institutes of Health. Swiss-Prot, along with its automatically curated supplement TrEMBL, merged with the Protein Information Resource protein database to create the UniProt Knowledgebase. This resource is recognized as the most comprehensive global repository of protein information. The UniProt Knowledgebase currently contains 263,525 entries in its manually curated Swiss-Prot section and 4,232,122 entries in its automatically annotated TrEMBL section. The UniProt consortium has developed three distinct database components, each tailored for specific applications: 1. The UniProt Knowledgebase (UniProtKB), which combines Swiss-Prot and TrEMBL, serves as the central resource for protein sequence and functional information. 2. The UniProt Non-redundant Reference (UniRef) databases, which cluster closely related sequences into single records to enhance the efficiency of similarity searches. 3. The UniProt Archive (UniParc), which acts as a comprehensive repository of protein sequences, preserving the historical record of all protein sequences.
